4	\subsection{Metric-Dependent Collapse: Format vs.\ Semantic}
5	\label{sec:format_vs_semantic}
6	
7	Diversity collapse under reward curation is real but mischaracterized by standard embedding-based metrics. Semantic diversity as measured by Vendi Score remains stable across generations (Section~\ref{sec:no_collapse}), yet surface-level formatting undergoes substantial homogenization. Table~\ref{tab:format_collapse} presents format diversity metrics for the LoRA $K{=}8$ curated condition (C2) and the LoRA random baseline (C5) across Gen~0 and Gen~2. Opening unique ratio, defined as the fraction of responses with a unique first 50 characters, drops from 0.701 to 0.367 under curation and from 0.794 to 0.513 under the random baseline. Opening entropy (Shannon entropy over first-10-token sequences, in bits) declines by 1.13 bits under curation versus 0.75 bits under the baseline. The near-duplicate start rate (fraction of responses sharing a 50-character prefix with at least one other response) rises from 50\% to 84\% under curation and from 38\% to 75\% under the baseline. Both conditions converge toward template-like openings, but curation accelerates this convergence and reaches a higher terminal repetition level. The absolute near-duplicate rates reflect different candidate pool sizes ($K{=}8$ vs.\ $K{=}4$); we focus on the generation-over-generation degradation rate within each condition, which controls for this difference.

tool_args.new_string: Diversity collapse under iterative self-training is real but mischaracterized by standard embedding-based metrics. Semantic diversity as measured by Vendi Score remains stable across generations (Section~\ref{sec:no_collapse}), yet surface-level formatting undergoes substantial homogenization. Table~\ref{tab:format_collapse} presents format diversity metrics for the LoRA $K{=}4$ curated condition (C1) and the LoRA $K{=}4$ random baseline (C5) across Gen~0 and Gen~2. Opening unique ratio, defined as the fraction of responses with a unique first 50 characters, drops from 0.757 to 0.477 under curation and from 0.753 to 0.479 under the random baseline. Opening entropy (Shannon entropy over first-10-token sequences, in bits) declines by 0.75 bits under both conditions. The near-duplicate start rate (fraction of responses sharing a 50-character prefix with at least one other response) rises from 37.9\% to 75.6\% under curation and from 38.3\% to 74.9\% under the baseline. Both conditions exhibit nearly identical degradation trajectories, which indicates that format collapse is an intrinsic property of iterative self-training rather than a consequence of reward curation. The C2 condition ($K{=}8$) provides further evidence: its opening entropy drops by 1.13 bits, compared to 0.75 bits for both $K{=}4$ conditions. Doubling $K$ amplifies homogenization, suggesting that candidate pool size acts as a scaling factor for format collapse. More candidates per prompt increase the probability of selecting responses that share common structural patterns, reinforcing template convergence across generations.

tool_args.old_string: The mechanism behind this format convergence is implicit preference bias in the reward model. ArmoRM assigns higher scores to responses that begin with certain structural patterns (e.g., numbered lists, direct answer statements). Iterative selection amplifies these initially mild biases: a slightly preferred opening template appears more often in the curated training set, the fine-tuned model generates it more frequently in the next generation, and it receives further preferential selection. This feedback loop operates on surface formatting while leaving semantic content largely untouched. Per-response type-token ratio (TTR), which measures lexical diversity within individual responses, drops by only 0.008 under curation compared to 0.023 under random selection. The reward model selects for format templates without constraining the vocabulary or topic coverage within those templates.
tool_args.new_string: The mechanism behind this format convergence is iterative self-training itself. When a model trains on its own outputs, the most frequent structural patterns in the current generation are slightly overrepresented in the training data. The fine-tuned model then generates these patterns more often, producing a new training set where the same templates are further concentrated. This self-reinforcing loop operates on surface formatting while leaving semantic content untouched, and it proceeds at the same rate regardless of whether the training data is reward-curated or randomly selected. Candidate pool size $K$ amplifies the loop: with more candidates per prompt, the probability of encountering and selecting responses with common opening patterns increases, producing faster template convergence. Per-response type-token ratio (TTR), which measures lexical diversity within individual responses, drops by only 0.012 under curation compared to 0.023 under random selection, confirming that the effect is confined to structural formatting rather than vocabulary or topic coverage.

50	\label{sec:measurement_implications}
51	
52	Standard diversity evaluation in iterative self-training relies on embedding-based metrics (Vendi Score, Self-BLEU, nearest-neighbor distance) that are insensitive to format-level homogenization. A typical evaluation workflow computes one or more of these metrics, observes stability, and concludes that diversity is maintained. Our results show that this workflow misses an entire dimension of output collapse. Format diversity metrics reveal progressive homogenization that is invisible to embedding-based evaluation, yet clearly perceptible to human readers who encounter repetitive opening patterns across model outputs.
53	
54	We propose two complementary metrics for format diversity monitoring in iterative training. Opening entropy measures the Shannon entropy over first-10-token sequences across a response corpus; a declining value indicates convergence toward template openings. Near-duplicate start rate measures the fraction of responses sharing a 50-character prefix with at least one other response; a rising value indicates increasing repetition of opening patterns. Both metrics require only string operations (no embedding model, no GPU), are interpretable without reference distributions, and capture a failure mode orthogonal to what semantic diversity metrics detect. In our experiments, opening entropy drops 0.75 bits under the $K{=}4$ conditions (intensifying to 1.13 bits under $K{=}8$) while Vendi Score changes by only $-$0.27\%, and near-duplicate start rate rises 38 percentage points while Self-BLEU remains below 0.007. These divergent trajectories confirm that the two metric families probe independent dimensions of the output distribution.
55
